clue.text: Where to expect bias in approaching Jack

definitions.text: Where to expect bias in approaching Jack

parts.words: Where to expect bias in approaching Jack
parts.note: in the game of bowls each ball is weighted on one side, its bias, and is rolled to curve towards the small white target ball called the jack

explanation.surface: A warning about where prejudice lies when you go up to talk to a man called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bias' and 'Jack' read as prejudice and a person; in bowls, a British lawn game, they are the weighted side of the ball and the target ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The lawn where bowls is played is where weighted balls curve towards the jack.

clue.text: Man of Calais at Westminster

parts.note: Rodin's statue group of six citizens of Calais stands in Victoria Tower Gardens beside the Houses of Parliament at Westminster

explanation.surface: A Frenchman visiting the British parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: A cast of Rodin's 'The Burghers of Calais' stands beside Parliament in Westminster, London.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a town, one of Rodin's six from Calais, is a freeman of that borough.

clue.text: Be uncertain who might signal a greeting

definitions.meaning: one who waves a hand in greeting

explanation.surface: Someone unsure whether to wave hello.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate is to hesitate, and a person flapping a hand in hello is one who waves.

clue.text: Laputans were these and fliers, too

definitions.text: Laputans were these and fliers, too

parts.words: Laputans were these and fliers, too
parts.note: in Gulliver's Travels Laputa is a flying island, so its people were both island dwellers and fliers

explanation.surface: A remark about Swift's Laputans being airmen as well.
explanation.walkthrough: Laputa, in Swift's Gulliver's Travels, is an island that floats in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of an island, here a floating one, are its natives.

clue.text: Down the rushy " (Allingham)

parts.note: fill the gap in William Allingham's poem 'The Fairies': 'Up the airy mountain, Down the rushy ...'

explanation.surface: A line of Allingham's verse with its last word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank from Allingham's poem 'The Fairies'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is a narrow Scottish or Irish valley, rhyming with 'men' in the poem.

clue.text: Puritan's surprising reincarnation

indicators.note: a reincarnation brings the same stuff back in a new body, and a surprising one rearranges the letters of Puritan's

explanation.surface: A strict Puritan unexpectedly reborn as someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging PURITANS gives the debauched Russian 'holy man', the surprising opposite of a puritan.
explanation.definitionFit: The notorious mystic at the Romanov court was a licentious holy man, an ironic rebirth of a strict moralist.

clue.text: Make legal bar available for poets

indicators.note: letters made available for a new use can be rearranged, so the word poets is reworked

explanation.surface: Making the bar legal and open to poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'available' rearranges POETS. 'bar' here is a verb: in law, to prevent someone from asserting a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, estoppel precludes a party from going back on an earlier statement, so the verb means to prevent legally.

clue.text: When to get on in a tight situation

indicators.note: one word goes inside another, so on is placed in tight

explanation.surface: Advice to climb aboard while things are cramped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a tight situation' reads as being in trouble; only 'in' works as the container signal, and 'When' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This evening is a time, answering the question 'when?'.

clue.text: Oberon administered one to Titania

parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream Oberon lifts the love spell on Titania with a counter-herb

explanation.surface: The fairy king gave his queen a dose of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Oberon used 'Dian's bud' to undo the love-juice that made Titania dote on Bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A counter-remedy undoes the effect of a poison or spell, as Oberon's herb did.

clue.text: Explosive lover returning to French poetry

definitions.note: used as a noun phrase for things that fire explosive charges, i.e. firearms

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the word lover is read backwards

parts.note: vers is the French word for verse

explanation.surface: A volatile lover goes back to French verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns LOVER into REVOL, then add VERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols with rotating chambers fire their rounds by exploding powder, so they are explosive weapons.

clue.text: In a fix with the eleventh man apparently missing ?

definitions.text: In a fix with the eleventh man apparently missing ?

parts.words: In a fix with the eleventh man apparently missing
parts.note: a woodworking peg sits fixed in its mortise, and a cricket team of eleven with one man missing has only ten players on the field

explanation.surface: A cricket side in trouble because a player has failed to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as TEN ON: ten men on the field, the eleventh absent. 'In a fix' is the joint, where the projecting piece is fixed into its slot.
explanation.definitionFit: A projecting peg on one piece of wood is fixed into a hole in another to make a joint.

clue.text: North Shore birds in flight

indicators.note: letters in flight are scattered, so North's N and the word Shore are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Birds flying along a northern coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in flight' scrambles N plus SHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-legged wading birds of the genus Ardea are a family of waterbirds.

clue.text: He's short and fat, to put it broadly

definitions.text: He's short and fat, to put it broadly

parts.words: He's short and fat, to put it broadly
parts.note: a ball of boiled dough is also a colloquial name for a short chubby person, and 'broadly' hints at plain speech and width

explanation.surface: A blunt description of a stout little man.
explanation.definitionFit: A plump, rounded person is called after the round lump of boiled dough.

clue.text: Burns's eruptions grew green !

parts.note: skin eruptions are red outbreaks; in Robert Burns's song 'Green Grow the ..., O' the Scots word means rushes, the plants that grow green

explanation.surface: Skin irritations from burns turning a sickly green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' looks like injuries from heat; it is the Scottish poet Robert Burns, whose Scots word for rushes is also the word for spots on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Outbreaks of red spots are skin eruptions, and the same word is Scots for rushes in Burns's song.

clue.text: One way to surmount a hurdle is to bestride it

definitions.text: One way to surmount a hurdle is to bestride it

parts.words: One way to surmount a hurdle is to bestride it
parts.note: sitting with legs on either side of something, or a high-jump style that rolls over the bar

explanation.surface: Advice on getting over an obstacle by climbing astride it.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing a leg on each side of something is to sit astride it, a way over a barrier.

clue.text: Rustic has a good deal of the devil's portion

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer or rustic
most means the greater part, a good deal

explanation.surface: A country fellow holds the bigger share of the devil's own lot.
explanation.walkthrough: From the saying 'devil take the hindmost': the last one is left to the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'devil take the hindmost' gives the last in line to the devil.

clue.text: Apollyon seems to have been of a reedy sort of build

indicators.note: to build is to put together, so the letters of reedy and sort are assembled anew

explanation.surface: The demon Apollyon looks to have had a slender, reed-like figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'build' rearranges REEDY and SORT. Apollyon, in Revelation, is the angel of the abyss; his name means 'the destroyer' in Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollyon's Greek name translates as the one who ruins or lays waste.

clue.text: Guinevere of Wales

parts.note: the Arthurian queen's name came from the Welsh Gwenhwyfar, whose Cornish form gives a modern girl's name

explanation.surface: King Arthur's queen, from Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The modern girl's name derives from the Celtic original of the Arthurian queen's name.

clue.text: Terribly cold charmer got rid of ?

parts.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian legend, an enchanting creature
shed means discarded or got rid of

explanation.surface: A freezing fairy has been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: A peri is a beautiful spirit in Persian myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling very cold, as in 'I'm frozen through', is a common British usage.

clue.text: Fish cake makes the dog pine

definitions.note: two senses: a butterfish of the Indian Ocean, and a liquorice sweet from Pontefract

parts.note: a pom is a Pomeranian, a small dog
fret means to pine or worry

explanation.surface: A fishcake that leaves the dog longing for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A Pomfret cake is a small round liquorice sweet from Pontefract in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a flat edible sea fish and a Yorkshire liquorice sweet.

clue.text: " Had pity on the least of things upon a chair" (Yeats)

definitions.text: " Had pity on the least of things upon a chair" (Yeats)

parts.words: Had pity on the least of things upon a chair
parts.note: fill the gap in a Yeats line about pity for a small creature sleeping on a chair

explanation.surface: A quotation from Yeats with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: the missing word in the line from W. B. Yeats's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Yeats's line describes the small creature as sleeping.

clue.text: Gave a toast to uncle

definitions.meaning: used as a verb: to take something to 'uncle', slang for the pawnbroker

explanation.surface: A nephew drinking to the health of an uncle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, so to pawn something is to put it with uncle.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking a health and pawning goods both use the verb meaning to promise or hand over as security.

clue.text: Do-gooder, bottled !

parts.note: a remedy does you good and is often sold in a bottle; 'bottled' also suggests a drunk do-gooder

explanation.surface: A busybody philanthropist who has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do-gooder' suggests a meddling person; here it is something that does you good, and 'bottled' is how it comes.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy taken for illness does the patient good and comes from the chemist in a bottle.

clue.text: The miser's hoard ?

parts.note: a hidden store; its name sounds like the money a miser piles up

explanation.surface: Asking what a miser keeps.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden store of valuables is a secret stash, and the word sounds like money.

clue.text: The stuff for the cold ?

parts.note: a coarse woollen cloth for winter coats, whose name sounds like the word for turning icy

explanation.surface: Asking what remedy to take for a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' means cloth: a heavy napped wool fabric, its name sounding like the word for going to ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy woollen cloth was used for warm coats, so it is material for cold weather.

clue.text: Job's interlocutor took root in America

definitions.text: Job's interlocutor took root in America

parts.words: Job's interlocutor took root in America
parts.note: the young man who speaks to Job in the Book of Job shares his first name with Root, the American Secretary of State

explanation.surface: One of Job's comforters settled in the New World.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took root' points to the American statesman Elihu Root, who shares the name of Job's fourth interlocutor.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest speaker in the Book of Job addresses Job after his three friends fall silent.

clue.text: Earn a thousand dollars on the football field

definitions.note: the definition points to a position on the pitch rather than naming it

parts.note: to win is to earn or gain
G, for grand, is slang for a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: Making a thousand dollars as a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide attacking position on the flank of the pitch is a player's place.

clue.text: The priest is in church and this is in the shrine

definitions.note: the definition describes the thing rather than naming it: an object kept in a shrine

indicators.note: one piece is in another, so the priest goes inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic, a church
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: The priest is inside the church, and a holy object is inside the shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs the two halves; the definition describes the thing kept in a shrine rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint's bone or belonging is venerated and kept in a shrine.

clue.text: Delicate jewelry by Champignon?

definitions.note: the definition names what the champignon mushroom makes rather than naming the thing itself

parts.note: fairy can mean delicate or dainty, like a fairy
a ring is a piece of jewelry

explanation.surface: Fine jewellery made by a craftsman named Champignon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champignon' looks like a jeweller's name; it is the mushroom Marasmius oreades, which grows in circles on lawns.
explanation.definitionFit: The champignon mushroom grows in a dark circle on grass, a circle folklore says elves danced.

clue.text: Calliope accompanies this example of 9

parts.note: a calliope is a steam organ heard at fairgrounds, and the ride it plays for is a turning machine, an example of the things in 9 across

explanation.surface: The Muse Calliope is accompanying an example from nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calliope' looks like the Muse of epic poetry; it is a steam organ. 9 across is REVOLVERS, here things that revolve.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground carousel turns round and round to steam-organ music, so it revolves.
